messages.author: f77d46b4bbd7a974
messages.subject: qplot: Howto draw the value of the points beside it in terms of  y-axis into the graph
parts:
Here's my code

a <- c(10000,12000,34000,35000,25000,50000,80000,7000)
b <- c(.1,.25,.5,.75,.9)
d <- quantile(a,b)

p <- c(10,25,50,75,90)
dframe <- data.frame(percentages=p,salaries=d)

qplot(x=p,y=d,data=dframe,ylab="Monthly Salaries",xlab="Salary
Percentile(%)",geom=c("point","line"),main="Salaries",xlim =
c(0,100),colour=I(alpha("orange",1/2)))

parts:
Hi, how about this one:

qplot(x=p,y=d,label=d, hjust=-0.25, data=dframe,ylab="Monthly
Salaries",xlab="Salary Percentile(%)",geom=c("point","line",
"text"),main="Salaries",xlim = c(0,100),colour=I(alpha("orange",1/2)))

if you want to control the graph in more detail, consider using
ggplot() instead of qplot().

messages.subject: Re: qplot: Howto draw the value of the points beside it in terms of  y-axis into the graph
parts:
This seemed to work for me. I put label in the aes() of ggplot and added ggp+ to each of the other geom() lines.

ggp <- ggplot(data=dframe,aes(x=p,y=d,label=d,group=dframe
$percentages,col=dframe$percentages))
ggp <- ggp+geom_line()
ggp <- ggp+geom_point()
ggp <- ggp+geom_text()
ggp


Not sure if it's what you want or not. 

You need to add your geoms to the original plot otherwise you'll just overwrite the other geoms.

Mic, 

I'm not terribly great at this either, but it looks like instead of  "group=dframe" you need data=dframe

ggp <- ggplot(data=dframe,aes(p, d,label=d, data=dframe

$percentages,col=dframe$percentages))
ggp <- ggp+geom_line()
ggp <- ggp+geom_point()
ggp <- ggp+geom_text()
ggp
That seems to work for me. It'd look better if you could offset the text though. Maybe shrink the font too.
